item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33584

📰
Comment
by Ambassador Albert P. Khorev
on an article by Romanian Ambassador
(published in “The Nation” newspaper on November 24, 2026)
✍️
I took note of the article published by the Romanian Ambassador to Pakistan on the occasion of Romania’s Armed Forces Day. The article extols the role of the Romanian Army in liberating the country from Nazi occupation during World War II, yet
makes not a single mention of the Soviet Army, which made the decisive contribution to liberating Romania from German forces.
It would appear that this “oversight” was not an innocent mistake, but rather a deliberate attempt to rewrite history in line with current foreign policy considerations.
I do not in any way seek to diminish the contribution of Romanian citizens who, following Romania’s decision to join the anti-Hitler coalition in August 1944, took part in the fight against Nazi Germany. At the same time, I consider it my duty to remind readers that it was the Red Army that bore the brunt of the fighting to liberate Romanian territory from Nazi occupation.
❗️
Soviet forces suffered a total of 286,000 casualties during the battles for Romania’s liberation.
To overlook their sacrifice in this context is simply outrageous and hypocritical.
It is noteworthy that, unlike the current head of Romania’s diplomatic mission in Pakistan, Romania’s wartime leadership openly acknowledged the Soviet Union’s contribution to the liberation of their country.
✍️
In March 1945, King Michael I of Romania wrote:
“I turn my thoughts to the glorious Soviet soldiers who sacrificed their lives for our sacred land. Their sacrifices will forever remain indelibly etched in the memory of all Romanians and will forever strengthen the bonds of friendship between our peoples.”
To this day, Soviet soldiers who gave their lives for the freedom of the Romanian people lie buried in cemeteries in 171 localities across Romania. I have no doubt that the Ambassador is well aware of this fact.
❗️
Equally hypocritical are the Romanian diplomat’s accusations that Russia is engaged in “aggression,” particularly given Bucharest’s support for NATO’s concept of forward defence on the alliance’s eastern flank – or, put more plainly, the deliberate expansion of NATO’s military activity near Russia’s borders.
👉
I would like to remind readers that it was NATO’s eastward expansion, in violation of guarantees given to Moscow, rather than any mythical “Russian aggression,” that undermined the European security architecture.
The expansion of the alliance’s military infrastructure, the staging of large-scale anti-Russian military exercises and NATO’s persistent efforts to stoke military hysteria are the real causes of the current crisis in Europe, the repercussions of which are being felt far beyond the continent, including in South Asia.
In conclusion, I would like to emphasize that disagreements over current political issues cannot justify the distortion of historical truth.
The memory of those who gave their lives to liberate Romania must not be held hostage to political expediency.
We know that many Romanians continue to honor that memory, particularly those who reject the events that took place before August 1944.

Due to the ultimatum issued by Latvia demanding the dismissal of all locally hired staff of the Department of Social Welfare at the Consular Department of the Russian Embassy in Riga (hereinafter the DSW),
on November 23, the Russian Foreign Ministry
summoned
Latvia’s Chargé d’Affaires ad interim Ramona Krasovska.
The Foreign Ministry explained the nature of the problems that will arise for the diplomatic missions of both countries, to the diplomat –
the main problem being the inability to continue paying military pensions
as they are processed by the DSW staff as per the Agreement Between the Government of the Russian Federation and the Government of the Republic of Latvia on the Social Protection of Russian Military Pensioners and Their Families Residing in the Republic of Latvia, signed on April 30, 1994 (hereinafter the “Agreement”).
The diplomat received
a corresponding note detailing Russia’s initiatives
regarding the resumption of talks on the employment of locally hired staff by the Latvian Embassy in Moscow in strict compliance with Russian law.
It was also proposed to the Latvian side that
consultations may be conducted on potential amendments to the Agreement and clarification of the status of the DSW staff
, provided that their dismissal would make it impossible to continue with the mechanism introduced by the Agreement and would considerably hinder the fulfilment of the obligations to
almost 6,000 military pensioners
and their family members (both Latvian and Russian citizens) residing in Latvia.
☝️
The official Riga was addressed with
an appeal to evaluate the humanitarian consequences
of the step it has requested, considering that
the pension is the only source of income
for many of the beneficiaries, and it is important to prevent any serious social issues in the lives of the elderly residents who belong to one of the most vulnerable population categories.

#Victory81
On November 24, 1944, the Red Army’s Baltic strategic offensive operation concluded, resulting in complete liberation of the Soviet Baltic republics — the Estonian SSR, the Latvian SSR and most of the territory of the Lithuanian SSR — from the Nazi invaders.
During this large-scale summer-autumn offensive on the north-western sector of the Soviet-German Front in 1944, our forces
inflicted a crushing defeat on the enemy:
the Nazi Army Group 'North' was effectively destroyed. Its remnants were encircled in what became known as the 'Courland Pocket' and finally eliminated in the spring of 1945.
The Baltic strategic offensive culminated in the
Moonsund landing operation
— an assault on enemy positions in the
#Moonsund
Archipelago, north-west of the Estonian SSR, which resulted in the complete expulsion of Nazi troops from the islands of Ösel (known as Saaremaa), Dagö (Hiiumaa) and Moon (Muhu) .
The total defeat of Nazi hordes in the Baltic region enabled the Red Army to launch its offensive in
East Prussia — the stronghold of German militarism,
where substantial enemy troops on the Eastern Front were concentrated.
***
On
September 14, 1944,
the forces of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Baltic Fronts launched an offensive in the Riga direction. The Red Army advanced rapidly,
breaching German defences
along the entire line of contact. In the first three days of the operation alone, Soviet strike forces advanced up to 50 kilometres. On
September
22
, the occupants were expelled from Tallinn, and on
October 13
— from Riga.
The
Baltic national units also made a significant contribution
to the liberation of the region from Nazi occupation and to our common Victory over Hitler's Reich.
✍️
From Marshal
Ivan
Bagramyan’
s memoirs on the conclusion of the Baltic Operation (
Thus We Advanced Towards Victory
):
Soviet soldiers achieved an outstanding victory <...>, demonstrating exceptional skills, mass heroism and unwavering devotion to their Motherland in battle.
The soldiers of national military formations — the 16th Lithuanian Rifle Division, the 130th Latvian Rifle Corps and the 8th Estonian Rifle Corps — fought for their land with tremendous enthusiasm and outstanding courage.
During the liberation of Soviet Baltic territories, the
Red Army destroyed 26 (!) Nazi divisions
and inflicted a crushing defeat on Army Group 'North' — the Reich’s main striking force in the Baltics. The remnants of the enemy troops were
cut off from the main Wehrmacht units in East Prussia
and subsequently completely destroyed by Soviet forces.
#NoStatuteOfLimitations
◾️
Following the Nazi invasion of the Baltic region in the summer of 1941, instead of the "independence" promised to Estonians, Latvians and Lithuanians, the
Nazis imposed an occupation regime
in the seized Soviet republics and pursued a policy of
terror and genocide.
With the arrival of German troops,
ultranationalists
and members of local
pro-fascist organisations who had sworn allegiance to Hitler
emerged from the shadows in occupied Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia.
They were known for their
atrocities
and the dirty work
on behalf of the Germans: they shot civilians, burned down villages,
perpetrated mass killings,
readily enlisted as guards and staff at concentration camps, and played an active role in the
extermination of the Jewish population
. These executioners had the blood of hundreds of thousands of civilians and prisoners of war on their hands.
Today's
Baltic regimes glorify these criminals
at the state level. Memorials are erected in honour of Nazi executioners, gatherings of SS legionnaires are organised, and Hitler's accomplices and their followers are publicly honoured.
❗️
Desecration of the sacred memory, cherished by our compatriots, of the Great Feat of Soviet soldiers-liberators, who laid down their lives to save the peoples of Europe from Nazi enslavement, has, regrettably, become the new norm among the political elites of the Baltic states.

🏔
#OTD
in 1730,
Alexander #Suvorov
was born in Moscow.
A soldier of the Imperial Guard who rose to the rank of Generalissimo, he became perhaps
the most celebrated commander in Russian military history
and
one of the best-known generals in the world
.
As a boy, Alexander loved listening to his father’s stories of
Peter the Great
, whom he had served, and of
Russia’s Northern War with Sweden of 1700-1721
. Small in stature and often in poor health,
young Suvorov dreamed of joining the army
, though his family doubted he could withstand the demands of a soldier’s life.
Nonetheless, he began his career in the Guards and went on to serve in
the Seven Years’ War
,
the wars against the Ottoman Empire
,
the Polish campaigns
and
the wars with France
.
It was during
the Russo-Turkish wars
under Catherine the Great that Suvorov earned his reputation as Russia’s finest general.
His victories at
Focsani
and
Rymnik
in 1789 brought him the title of
Count Rymniksky
and
the Order of St George, First Class
. Among his honours was a diamond-studded sword bearing the inscription
“To the Victor over the Grand Vizier”
. Five years later, following the Polish campaign of 1794, he became
a field marshal
.
✍️
Suvorov was also a gifted teacher who trained a generation of senior Russian officers.
In his book
The Science of Winning
, a practical guide for officers and soldiers, he set down the lessons of a lifetime in the field. He expected his officers to exercise their own judgement and think on their feet when faced with the unexpected. For the ordinary soldier, he summed up the value of rigorous training in a few memorable words:
“
Train hard and the march will be easy”
.
Suvorov is renowned for having fought more than 60 battles without losing a single one.
His campaigns took him across what are now
at least eight European countries
, from the banks of the Rymnik in present-day Romania to the plains of northern Italy.
His final military campaign
took him across the Swiss Alps.
In September 1799, his troops crossed
the St Gotthard Pass
and fought their way through the Schöllenen Gorge at the Devil’s Bridge. After the Italian and Swiss campaigns, Paul I conferred on him the rank of
Generalissimo
. Suvorov
died in St Petersburg
the following year.
🇷🇺
🇨🇭
On September 26, 1898
, the Suvorov Cross,
one of the most striking memorials to the Russian commander
, was unveiled in Switzerland’s Schöllenen Gorge.
Carved into the sheer rock face near the Devil’s Bridge,
the 12-metre-high cross
commemorates the Russian soldiers who lost their lives crossing the Alps.
To this day, Russians living in Switzerland and their Swiss friends
gather at the foot of the cross
to honour the memory of the great commander and his men.
#RussianHistory
#MilitaryHistory

Sergey Lavrov
will pay

the annual joint meeting of the boards of
the Russian Foreign Ministry
and
the Belarusian Foreign Ministry
.

the Treaty on the Establishment of the Union State
, which the two countries signed in December 1999.

the Programme of Coordinated Foreign Policy Action for 2024-2026
of the states parties to the Treaty on the Establishment of the Union State. Under the programme, Russia and Belarus
closely coordinate

jointly advance
their shared interests on the international stage.
The boards will also discuss
how to align the two countries’ approaches to work at the
#UN
and across the UN system
, how their diplomatic services can help Russian and Belarusian regions strengthen interregional and cross-border cooperation, and how the two countries can respond jointly to crises and emergencies.
Following the meeting, the two Sides will sign
a new Programme of Coordinated Foreign Policy Action for 2027-2029
and submit it to the Supreme State Council of the Union State for approval. They will also sign
a joint resolution of the two boards
and
a plan for consultations
between the Foreign Ministries in 2027.
On the sidelines of the meeting,
Sergey Lavrov
will hold talks with Foreign Minister of Belarus
Maxim Ryzhenkov
on current issues in bilateral cooperation and on further integration within the Union State. The Ministers will also exchange views on key international issues.
Sergey Lavrov’s visit will include
a series of commemorative events
. Together with his Belarusian counterpart,
he will lay flowers at the Eternal Flame
in memory of those who defended Belarus during
the Great Patriotic War of 1941-1945
. He will also attend the unveiling of a bust of
Nikolai Rumyantsev
, Foreign Minister of the Russian Empire, who was buried 200 years ago in Gomel’s Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul. The commemorations will also honour Soviet Foreign Minister
Andrey Gromyko
, who was born 117 years ago in the Gomel district.
***
#RussiaBelarus
The Republic of Belarus is Russia’s closest ally and strategic partner
. The two countries share longstanding traditions of friendship and mutual assistance, close cultural and spiritual ties, a common history and prospects for the future.
🇷🇺
🇧🇾
Relations between Russia and Belarus
can serve as a model for cooperation between states on an equal and mutually beneficial basis
. The level of cooperation the two countries have achieved within the Union State can also serve as a benchmark for other integration groupings across Eurasia.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33576

🇷🇺
Statement by the delegation of the Russian Federation at
the High-Level Panel on the Occasion of the 30th Anniversary of
the CTBT
📍
Vienna, 23 November 2026
💬
When the CTBT was adopted in 1996 all those who were part of the process of its development and those countries acceded to the Treaty later shared a sincere common commitment to end nuclear testing worldwide. From the very beginning
the CTBT was conceived as a unique instrument
which would comprehensively ban all types of such activities.
Russia signed the Treaty in 1996 and ratified it in 2000. Since then
we spared no political effort in order to contribute to early entry into force of the CTBT
.
Unfortunately,
30 years after the Treaty is still not in force and prospects of it are very gloomy
. On the contrary we witness that some of the important countries that were the driving force behind development of the Treaty not only abandoned efforts to ratify it but openly criticize the CTBT and its verification mechanism.
Nevertheless, the commitment to end nuclear testing has definitely not disappeared. We can see this commitment first of all in those who work in the Provisional Technical Secretariat of the Preparatory Commission. Vivid example
is recent successful conduct of
Integrated Field Exercise in Namibia
which is an important milestone in developing On-Site Inspections capabilities
. These exercises provide an opportunity to test inspection procedures under realistic field conditions, strengthen operational readiness and enhance technical expertise in order to have a robust verification instrument once Treaty is in force.
Another unprecedented technical and scientific achievement is
the International Monitoring System
designed to comprise 321 monitoring stations and 16 radionuclide laboratories. Together with
the International Data Centre
it represents a unique mechanism that provides States Signatories with timely and objective information for the analysis of the events potentially relevant to compliance of the CTBT.
We believe that the main objective of all those who really care about the Treaty and a commitment to end nuclear testing should be
to preserve the architecture of the CTBT as it is
for the future when international conditions may become more conducive for its entry into force. Ideas about fixing or somehow rebalancing the components of the CTBT will definitely not bring us closer to the entry into force but rather they pose the risk of losing the valuable instruments of the Treaty.
Important role in preserving the CTBT and guarding it against destructive influence lies with
its Article XIV process
. A balanced, forward-looking and inclusive Final Declaration, reflecting the legitimate interests of all States, would make a far more meaningful contribution to our common objective. Thirty years of the CTBT have demonstrated what the international community can achieve through multilateral cooperation, scientific progress and a shared commitment to international security.

✉️
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
message of greetings
to Director General of the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation Gerd Müller
(November 23, 2026)
✍️
Please accept my sincere congratulations on
the 60th anniversary
of
the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation
(
#UNIDO
).
Over the past six decades, UNIDO has come a long way, establishing itself as
the leading specialised agency within the UN system in the field of industrial development
.
It makes
a significant contribution
to strengthening
the productive capacities of developing countries,
modernising
industry, and
promoting
the dissemination of advanced technologies.
Its efforts to promote
industrialisation in African countries
, which account for more than half of the Organisation’s project activities are particularly noteworthy.
☝️
R
ussia and UNIDO have a long history of constructive and mutually beneficial cooperation dating back to the Soviet era.
Our country was among the Organisation’s founding members and has consistently supported efforts to strengthen its capabilities.
We highly value
the practical results
achieved through our joint efforts over the years.
With Russia’s support, projects have been implemented in such areas as
industrial modernisation, improving labour productivity at enterprises across Eurasia and Latin America, facilitating trade, and promoting high-quality products on international markets.
New opportunities for cooperation are emerging within the
#BRICS
framework
, including through the establishment of a BRICS Centre for Industrial Competencies with UNIDO’s participation.
We look forward to further developing our partnership
with a view to building a fair and sustainable system of international industrial cooperation based on the principles of equality, mutual respect and due consideration for the national priorities of states.
🤝
I wish the leadership and staff of UNIDO sound health, wellbeing, and continued success in fulfilling the Organisation’s mandate.
SERGEY LAVROV

item.title: ✍️ To all who have honoured the memory of Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America
item.description: To all who have honoured the memory of Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America ✍️ On behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, I would like to express my gratitude to all those who have sent us messages of condolence and support in connection with the untimely passing of the Russian Ambassador to the United States Alexander Nikitich Darchiev. For the staff, for the team of the Foreign Ministry, his passing is an irreplaceable loss. In Alexander Nikitich, we have lost not only a professional of the highest caliber, a renowned expert on American affairs, and an unwavering patriot of our country, but also a dear friend, a sensitive and attentive mentor, and a colleague who was always ready to assist and lend a helping hand. Alexander Darchiev devoted his entire life to selfless service to his homeland. May his memory live on! All condolences received have been conveyed to the family and loved ones of the deceased. SERGEY RYABKOV, Deputy Foreign Minister of Russia

To all who have honoured the memory of Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America
✍️
On behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, I would like to express my gratitude to all those
who have sent us messages of condolence and support
in connection with the untimely passing of the Russian Ambassador to the United States Alexander Nikitich Darchiev.
For the staff, for the team of the Foreign Ministry, his passing is
an irreplaceable loss.
In Alexander Nikitich, we have lost not only a professional of the highest caliber, a renowned expert on American affairs, and an unwavering patriot of our country, but also a dear friend, a sensitive and attentive mentor, and a colleague who was always ready to assist and lend a helping hand.
Alexander Darchiev devoted his entire life to selfless service to his homeland.
May his memory live on!
All condolences received have been conveyed to the family and loved ones of the deceased.
SERGEY RYABKOV, Deputy Foreign Minister of Russia
